newsitem.title: USA: GM profit margin gains still short of goal.
newsitem.headline: GM profit margin gains still short of goal.

text.p: General Motors Corp Chairman John Smith said Tuesday he is pleased with gains in the automaker's third quarter net profit margin, but said the company is still short of its goal for an average profit margin of five percent of the auto business cycle.

GM said its net profit margin from continuing operations was 3.7 percent, up from 1.3 percent. For North American Operations and Delphi Automotive Systems, the rate was a profit margin of 2.1 percent, compared to a loss margin of 0.4 percent a year ago. GM posted third quarter income from continuing operations of $1.27 billion, up from $396.7 million.
"We still have our work cut out to improve our margin performance," Smith said in a statement.
GM said its North American retail incentives for the third quarter were $764 per vehicle, compared with $530 a year ago. GM Europe spent $586 per vehicle, down from $656 in the year-ago period.

Dealers had a 77-day supply of GM cars on their lots at the end of the third quarter, down from 79 a year ago. Truck supply climbed to 99 days from 97 days. The industry generally considers a 60-day supply as ideal.

In his statement, Smith said GM's new product launches are on schedule. Production of GM's new full-size vans at its Wentzville, Mo., assembly plant and on the new Saturn coupe line in Spring Hill, Tenn., have reached full line speed.
"We're pleased that the launches are on track, especially considering the challenges of our tough vehicle-introduction schedule," he said.
Nine of GM's North American assembly plants are involved in the launch of 15 new cars and trucks for the U.S. and overseas.
